title: Are Microsoft’s AI plans being held back by a shortage of chips?
excerpt: Guardian investigation finds apparent discrepancy between what tech company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced chips it has in operation
content_html:
The chips are quite small and some can be held in the palm of a hand. They are fundamental to the development of artificial intelligence models – and the world’s biggest technology companies need vast numbers of them to keep ahead.

Microsoft is one of them. And, on paper, it seems to have a problem. A Guardian investigation has found an apparent discrepancy between what the company has said about its AI capacity – and the number of advanced AI chips it has in operation.

It is not a small shortfall either. Microsoft reportedly targeted having 1.8m AI chips installed in its datacentres around the globe by the end of 2024. Nearly two years on, in the middle of a $280bn (£208bn) expansion, the company has 2.2m AI chips installed, according to internal documents seen by the Guardian. This is less than half the number some experts had imagined.

Put simply, the global AI arms race requires a massive build-out of datacentres that run on extremely expensive chips. The apparent discrepancy over the chips suggests Microsoft’s newest datacentres may not be fully operational or, if they are, they do not have the chips they need.

This highlights something even more fundamental about charting the progress being made in the development of AI technologies. The chips that power AI are made by Nvidia, one of the two most valuable companies in the world. Its supply chain is one of the most tightly held secrets in the entire industry.

With almost no exceptions, Nvidia does not report how many of these chips it sells or to whom. Its clients, the world’s biggest tech companies, in turn do not reveal how many they have. Without this information, it is very hard for anyone to know whether AI is booming or not.

Microsoft: a power vacuum?

In the past two years, Microsoft says it has built AI infrastructure at breakneck speed. Its chief executive, Satya Nadella, said last year it would double its global datacentre footprint by mid-2027. Since 2022 it has ploughed roughly $280bn into the land, buildings and computational infrastructure to build AI. This includes more than $41bn in the past quarter.

But it is difficult to estimate how many datacentres Microsoft has built with this money.

It is possible to assess the progress that the company is making by looking at what it has announced publicly, with a particular eye on the power it needs. Datacentres need electricity, so one way of estimating how many datacentres are operational is to add up the energy Microsoft has at its disposal – its AI capacity.

Microsoft’s own claims, set out in annual reports and quarterly earnings, suggest it has added 5GW of datacentre capacity over the past two years as part of its AI build-out. It says it now has hundreds of datacentres on five continents.

Five gigawatts is a dizzying amount of energy – it is four times the size of the largest datacentre park in Europe. But Microsoft’s total capacity should be even greater than this; it has been building AI infrastructure since 2022. How much greater is an open question.

In an internal presentation from 2024, Microsoft reportedly claimed to have 5GW of datacentre capacity already installed. That would suggest it could now have a total of 10GW of capacity. It is unclear if all of these are AI datacentres – some could be for other cloud services. But Microsoft’s own statements indicate that the overwhelming focus of its capital expenditures in recent years has been to build AI infrastructure.

Ten gigawatts of AI datacentres would suggest Microsoft should have roughly 6.4m graphics processing units (GPUs). Shaolei Ren, a professor at the University of California, Riverside, said Microsoft’s sustainability reports, which contain figures for its electricity usage and are published separately from its financials, painted a different picture.

He said these reports suggest Microsoft’s AI capacity in 2024 was probably closer to 1.2GW. But even this lower figure would indicate Microsoft would need roughly 4m AI chips – if it added 5GW of AI datacentres in the past two years.

“According to their own metrics, Microsoft could be correct. But it isn’t clear what they mean when they say they have added datacentre capacity. They are giving insufficient context,” Ren said. “The sustainability reports are audited by a third party. They have more credibility than announcements.”

An analyst who specialises in Nvidia said they thought Microsoft would have more chips, given its public statements. “They’re low to me. They’re less than I expected Microsoft would have,” they said.

Microsoft insisted the Guardian’s calculations were based on incorrect information. It did not offer any insight as to which of the Guardian’s numbers were incorrect or why. What is clear is that Microsoft’s build-out of AI capacity appears to be going far more slowly than its annual reports may suggest.

Ren said: “It may be plausible to secure or announce 1GW of power capacity within a single quarter on paper. But bringing that capacity online and actually using it for computing within the same quarter would be far more difficult.”

Sources within Microsoft say the company’s total number of AI chips has “barely moved” over the past year.

Some of the apparent discrepancy may be explained by Microsoft’s tie-up with OpenAI. The exact terms of their commercial partnership are not public, but this unit may account for some of Microsoft’s datacentre deployments, which would not be in the documents the Guardian has seen.

‘You may have a bunch of chips … you can’t plug in’

There is another factor: some of Microsoft’s big projects appear to be far from operational.

Take Microsoft’s largest AI development in the US, a pair of datacentres in Wisconsin and Georgia called Fairwater. In April, Nadella, Microsoft’s chief executive, said the Fairwater project in Wisconsin “is going live”.

Satellite footage of the building from Epoch AI, however, appears to indicate only part of it is operational. In May, Microsoft admitted to a Wisconsin newspaper that Fairwater was not yet online.

This is very common, said Ren. Initially it was a multi-gigawatt, multibillion-dollar investment. Three years later, only 300MW has been built.

The internal document also indicates Microsoft has fewer of Nvidia’s newest model of chip, the Blackwell, than one might expect given Nvidia’s public announcements. Last March, Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, said orders for Blackwells from Nvidia’s top four customers – widely thought to be Amazon, Oracle, Microsoft and Google – amounted to 3.6m.

There was no breakdown given for this figure, but Microsoft has historically been one of Nvidia’s largest customers. If this was still the case, that should put Microsoft’s total Blackwell holdings at somewhere close to 1m chips. In fact, it has less than half of this amount installed.

Where are the chips, if not in the datacentres?

Nvidia’s balance sheets appear to indicate that it has sold a great many chips; it posted a revenue of $215.9bn in February. Has Microsoft bought these but not installed them? How many, and are all of them in its possession?

Nadella appeared to gesture at this question on a podcast late last year called All Things AI, where he talked about Microsoft’s datacentre build-out. The biggest problem, he said, was electrical power and building datacentres close enough to where power was located.

“If you can’t do that, you may actually have a bunch of chips sitting in inventory that I can’t plug in. In fact, that is my problem today. It’s not a supply issue of chips. It’s actually the fact that I don’t have warm shells to plug into.”

A Microsoft spokesperson said: “Over several decades, Microsoft has built a global infrastructure to meet rapidly growing customer demand for cloud and AI services. Our datacentres combine custom silicon, AMD, Intel and Nvidia chips across multiple generations with the networking, storage and systems infrastructure required to operate at scale.

“Microsoft does not report on the volume of specific chips in its AI infrastructure. The estimates the Guardian has shared with us are inaccurate, drawing the wrong conclusions from incorrect assumptions.”

Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.

How to calculate numbers of chips from a company’s ‘AI capacity’

The world’s biggest technology companies give figures for their AI capacity in terms of power: gigawatts. One gigawatt powers between 700,000 and 1m homes. Meta says its controversial Hyperion datacentre in Louisiana will have 5GW of capacity. The UK company DataVita is planning a 1GW datacentre in Lanarkshire.

Converting these figures into chips means calculating how many chips can be run with that amount of power. The Guardian used the following methodology, reviewing these calculations with Abdeltawab Hendawi, a professor at the University of Rhode Island, and Ren.

To get a very broad approximation of how many chips there are in a datacentre, you could divide the power usage of that datacentre by the power usage of an AI chip – for example, an H100. A single H100 uses 700W. If Microsoft has 10GW of capacity, dividing this by 700 watts suggests it should have 12m chips.

H100s make up the bulk of the chips described in the internal document. It also indicates that Microsoft has A100s, which use less power, and Blackwells, which use more.

But this approximation does not account for several factors. First, datacentres have cooling systems and other equipment, which also use electricity. Ren estimates that in a given AI datacentre, 80% of the electricity goes to computer chips. This is roughly in accordance with figures from the International Energy Agency, although the number depends on the efficiency of the datacentre. Eighty per cent of 10GW would suggest 8GW may actually be in use.

This is slightly lower than Microsoft’s own figures for its datacentre efficiency, which appear in a 2024 sustainability report and suggest that 89% of the electricity in its new datacentres powers the IT systems, with an 11% overhead.

Second, not all the chips in a datacentre are AI chips. Instead, AI chips are fitted on to server racks with other computer chips, such as memory chips, that help them run calculations. A server with eight H100 GPUs uses a maximum of about 10kW of power.

Dividing 8GW by 10kW gives 800,000 servers, or 6.4m chips.

This is a conservative estimate, as in practice companies such as Microsoft oversubscribe their power capacity to some extent – putting more chips in a datacentre than can be supported by their IT capacity, said Ren.

That would suggest it could now have a total of 10GW of capacity. It is unclear if all of these are AI datacentres – some could be for other cloud services. But Microsoft’s own statements indicate that the overwhelming focus of its capital expenditures in recent years has been to build AI infrastructure.

sentences.en: In an internal presentation from 2024, Microsoft reportedly claimed to have 5GW of datacentre capacity already installed.
sentences.zh: 据报道，在 2024 年的内部演示中，微软声称已经安装了 5GW 的数据中心容量。

sentences.en: That would suggest it could now have a total of 10GW of capacity.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它现在的总产能可能达到 10GW。

sentences.en: It is unclear if all of these are AI datacentres – some could be for other cloud services.
sentences.zh: 目前尚不清楚所有这些是否都是人工智能数据中心——有些可能用于其他云服务。

sentences.en: But Microsoft’s own statements indicate that the overwhelming focus of its capital expenditures in recent years has been to build AI infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 但微软自己的声明表明，近年来其资本支出的压倒性重点是建设人工智能基础设施。

blocks.html_en: Ten gigawatts of AI datacentres would suggest Microsoft should have roughly 6.4m graphics processing units (GPUs). Shaolei Ren, a professor at the University of California, Riverside, said Microsoft’s sustainability reports, which contain figures for its electricity usage and are published separately from its financials, painted a different picture.

sentences.en: Ten gigawatts of AI datacentres would suggest Microsoft should have roughly 6.4m graphics processing units (GPUs).
sentences.zh: 10 吉瓦的人工智能数据中心意味着微软应该拥有大约 640 万个图形处理单元 (GPU)。

sentences.en: Shaolei Ren, a professor at the University of California, Riverside, said Microsoft’s sustainability reports, which contain figures for its electricity usage and are published separately from its financials, painted a different picture.
sentences.zh: 加州大学河滨分校教授任少雷表示，微软的可持续发展报告包含了用电量数据，并且与财务数据分开发布，描绘了一幅不同的画面。

blocks.html_en: He said these reports suggest Microsoft’s AI capacity in 2024 was probably closer to 1.2GW. But even this lower figure would indicate Microsoft would need roughly 4m AI chips – if it added 5GW of AI datacentres in the past two years.

sentences.en: He said these reports suggest Microsoft’s AI capacity in 2024 was probably closer to 1.2GW.
sentences.zh: 他表示，这些报告表明微软 2024 年的人工智能产能可能接近 1.2GW。

sentences.en: But even this lower figure would indicate Microsoft would need roughly 4m AI chips – if it added 5GW of AI datacentres in the past two years.
sentences.zh: 但即使这个较低的数字也表明微软将需要大约 400 万个 AI 芯片——如果它在过去两年增加 5GW 的 AI 数据中心。

blocks.html_en: “According to their own metrics, Microsoft could be correct. But it isn’t clear what they mean when they say they have added datacentre capacity. They are giving insufficient context,” Ren said. “The sustainability reports are audited by a third party. They have more credibility than announcements.”

sentences.en: “According to their own metrics, Microsoft could be correct.
sentences.zh: “根据他们自己的指标，微软可能是正确的。

sentences.en: But it isn’t clear what they mean when they say they have added datacentre capacity.
sentences.zh: 但当他们说增加了数据中心容量时，尚不清楚他们的意思。

sentences.en: They are giving insufficient context,” Ren said.
sentences.zh: 他们没有提供足够的背景信息，”任说。

sentences.en: “The sustainability reports are audited by a third party.
sentences.zh: “可持续发展报告由第三方审核。

sentences.en: They have more credibility than announcements.”
sentences.zh: 它们比公告更有可信度。”

blocks.html_en: An analyst who specialises in Nvidia said they thought Microsoft would have more chips, given its public statements. “They’re low to me. They’re less than I expected Microsoft would have,” they said.

sentences.en: An analyst who specialises in Nvidia said they thought Microsoft would have more chips, given its public statements.
sentences.zh: 一位专门研究英伟达的分析师表示，鉴于微软的公开声明，他们认为微软将拥有更多芯片。

sentences.en: “They’re low to me.
sentences.zh: “他们对我来说很低。

sentences.en: They’re less than I expected Microsoft would have,” they said.
sentences.zh: 它们比我预期的微软要少，”他们说。

blocks.html_en: Microsoft insisted the Guardian’s calculations were based on incorrect information. It did not offer any insight as to which of the Guardian’s numbers were incorrect or why. What is clear is that Microsoft’s build-out of AI capacity appears to be going far more slowly than its annual reports may suggest.

sentences.en: Microsoft insisted the Guardian’s calculations were based on incorrect information.
sentences.zh: 微软坚称《卫报》的计算基于不正确的信息。

sentences.en: It did not offer any insight as to which of the Guardian’s numbers were incorrect or why.
sentences.zh: 它没有提供任何关于《卫报》的哪些数字不正确或原因的见解。

sentences.en: What is clear is that Microsoft’s build-out of AI capacity appears to be going far more slowly than its annual reports may suggest.
sentences.zh: 显而易见的是，微软人工智能能力的建设速度似乎比其年度报告显示的要慢得多。

blocks.html_en: Ren said: “It may be plausible to secure or announce 1GW of power capacity within a single quarter on paper. But bringing that capacity online and actually using it for computing within the same quarter would be far more difficult.”

sentences.en: Ren said: “It may be plausible to secure or announce 1GW of power capacity within a single quarter on paper.
sentences.zh: 任正非表示：“理论上，在一个季度内确保或宣布 1GW 的电力装机容量可能是合理的。

sentences.en: But bringing that capacity online and actually using it for computing within the same quarter would be far more difficult.”
sentences.zh: 但在同一季度内将该容量上线并实际用于计算将会困难得多。”

blocks.html_en: Sources within Microsoft say the company’s total number of AI chips has “barely moved” over the past year.

sentences.en: Sources within Microsoft say the company’s total number of AI chips has “barely moved” over the past year.
sentences.zh: 微软内部消息人士称，该公司的人工智能芯片总数在过去一年“几乎没有变化”。

blocks.html_en: Some of the apparent discrepancy may be explained by Microsoft’s tie-up with OpenAI. The exact terms of their commercial partnership are not public, but this unit may account for some of Microsoft’s datacentre deployments, which would not be in the documents the Guardian has seen.

sentences.en: Some of the apparent discrepancy may be explained by Microsoft’s tie-up with OpenAI.
sentences.zh: 一些明显的差异可能是由于微软与 OpenAI 的合作造成的。

sentences.en: The exact terms of their commercial partnership are not public, but this unit may account for some of Microsoft’s datacentre deployments, which would not be in the documents the Guardian has seen.
sentences.zh: 他们商业合作伙伴关系的具体条款并未公开，但该部门可能负责微软的一些数据中心部署，而《卫报》看到的文件中并没有这些内容。

sentences.en: A Microsoft datacentre in Middenmeer, the Netherlands.
sentences.zh: 位于荷兰 Middenmeer 的 Microsoft 数据中心。

sentences.en: Photograph: ANP/Shutterstock
sentences.zh: 照片：ANP/Shutterstock

blocks.html_en: ‘You may have a bunch of chips … you can’t plug in’

sentences.en: ‘You may have a bunch of chips …
sentences.zh: “你可能有一堆筹码……

sentences.en: you can’t plug in’
sentences.zh: 你无法插入”

blocks.html_en: There is another factor: some of Microsoft’s big projects appear to be far from operational.

sentences.en: There is another factor: some of Microsoft’s big projects appear to be far from operational.
sentences.zh: 还有另一个因素：微软的一些大型项目似乎远未投入运营。

blocks.html_en: Take Microsoft’s largest AI development in the US, a pair of datacentres in Wisconsin and Georgia called Fairwater. In April, Nadella, Microsoft’s chief executive, said the Fairwater project in Wisconsin “is going live”.

sentences.en: Take Microsoft’s largest AI development in the US, a pair of datacentres in Wisconsin and Georgia called Fairwater.
sentences.zh: 以微软在美国最大的人工智能开发项目为例，位于威斯康星州和佐治亚州的两个名为 Fairwater 的数据中心。

sentences.en: In April, Nadella, Microsoft’s chief executive, said the Fairwater project in Wisconsin “is going live”.
sentences.zh: 四月，微软首席执行官纳德拉表示，威斯康星州的 Fairwater 项目“即将上线”。

blocks.html_en: Satellite footage of the building from Epoch AI, however, appears to indicate only part of it is operational. In May, Microsoft admitted to a Wisconsin newspaper that Fairwater was not yet online.

sentences.en: Satellite footage of the building from Epoch AI, however, appears to indicate only part of it is operational.
sentences.zh: 然而，Epoch AI 拍摄的该建筑的卫星镜头似乎表明，该建筑仅部分可用。

sentences.en: In May, Microsoft admitted to a Wisconsin newspaper that Fairwater was not yet online.
sentences.zh: 今年五月，微软向威斯康星州一家报纸承认，Fairwater 尚未上线。

blocks.html_en: This is very common, said Ren. Initially it was a multi-gigawatt, multibillion-dollar investment. Three years later, only 300MW has been built.

sentences.en: This is very common, said Ren.
sentences.zh: 任正非说，这种情况很常见。

sentences.en: Initially it was a multi-gigawatt, multibillion-dollar investment.
sentences.zh: 最初这是一项数千兆瓦、数十亿美元的投资。

sentences.en: Three years later, only 300MW has been built.
sentences.zh: 三年后，仅建成300MW。

sentences.en: Satya Nadella said last year Microsoft would double its global datacentre footprint by mid-2027.
sentences.zh: 萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 去年表示，微软将在 2027 年中期之前将其全球数据中心足迹扩大一倍。

sentences.en: Photograph: Jeff Chiu/AP
sentences.zh: 摄影：Jeff Chiu/美联社

blocks.html_en: The internal document also indicates Microsoft has fewer of Nvidia’s newest model of chip, the Blackwell, than one might expect given Nvidia’s public announcements. Last March, Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, said orders for Blackwells from Nvidia’s top four customers – widely thought to be Amazon, Oracle, Microsoft and Google – amounted to 3.6m.

sentences.en: The internal document also indicates Microsoft has fewer of Nvidia’s newest model of chip, the Blackwell, than one might expect given Nvidia’s public announcements.
sentences.zh: 内部文件还表明，微软拥有的英伟达最新型号的芯片 Blackwell 数量比英伟达公开声明中的预期要少。

sentences.en: Last March, Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, said orders for Blackwells from Nvidia’s top four customers – widely thought to be Amazon, Oracle, Microsoft and Google – amounted to 3.6m.
sentences.zh: 去年 3 月，Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 表示，Nvidia 四大客户（普遍认为是亚马逊、甲骨文、微软和谷歌）对 Blackwells 的订单达到 360 万台。

blocks.html_en: There was no breakdown given for this figure, but Microsoft has historically been one of Nvidia’s largest customers. If this was still the case, that should put Microsoft’s total Blackwell holdings at somewhere close to 1m chips. In fact, it has less than half of this amount installed.

sentences.en: There was no breakdown given for this figure, but Microsoft has historically been one of Nvidia’s largest customers.
sentences.zh: 虽然没有给出这个数字的详细数据，但微软历来是英伟达最大的客户之一。

sentences.en: If this was still the case, that should put Microsoft’s total Blackwell holdings at somewhere close to 1m chips.
sentences.zh: 如果情况仍然如此，那么微软持有的 Blackwell 芯片总数应该接近 100 万块。

sentences.en: In fact, it has less than half of this amount installed.
sentences.zh: 事实上，它的安装量还不到这个数量的一半。

blocks.html_en: Where are the chips, if not in the datacentres?

sentences.en: Where are the chips, if not in the datacentres?
sentences.zh: 如果芯片不在数据中心，那么芯片在哪里？

blocks.html_en: Nvidia’s balance sheets appear to indicate that it has sold a great many chips; it posted a revenue of $215.9bn in February. Has Microsoft bought these but not installed them? How many, and are all of them in its possession?

sentences.en: Nvidia’s balance sheets appear to indicate that it has sold a great many chips; it posted a revenue of $215.9bn in February.
sentences.zh: 英伟达的资产负债表似乎表明它已经售出了大量芯片；该公司 2 月份营收为 2159 亿美元。

sentences.en: Has Microsoft bought these but not installed them?
sentences.zh: 微软购买了这些但没有安装它们吗？

sentences.en: How many, and are all of them in its possession?
sentences.zh: 有多少，全部都在它的手里吗？

blocks.html_en: Nadella appeared to gesture at this question on a podcast late last year called All Things AI, where he talked about Microsoft’s datacentre build-out. The biggest problem, he said, was electrical power and building datacentres close enough to where power was located.

sentences.en: Nadella appeared to gesture at this question on a podcast late last year called All Things AI, where he talked about Microsoft’s datacentre build-out.
sentences.zh: 纳德拉似乎在去年年底的一个名为 All Things AI 的播客中对这个问题做出了手势，他在其中谈到了微软的数据中心建设。

sentences.en: The biggest problem, he said, was electrical power and building datacentres close enough to where power was located.
sentences.zh: 他说，最大的问题是电力和在距离电力所在地足够近的地方建造数据中心。

blocks.html_en: “If you can’t do that, you may actually have a bunch of chips sitting in inventory that I can’t plug in. In fact, that is my problem today. It’s not a supply issue of chips. It’s actually the fact that I don’t have warm shells to plug into.”

sentences.en: “If you can’t do that, you may actually have a bunch of chips sitting in inventory that I can’t plug in.
sentences.zh: “如果你做不到这一点，你的库存中可能实际上有一堆我无法插入的芯片。

sentences.en: In fact, that is my problem today.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这就是我今天的问题。

sentences.en: It’s not a supply issue of chips.
sentences.zh: 这不是芯片供应问题。

sentences.en: It’s actually the fact that I don’t have warm shells to plug into.”
sentences.zh: 事实上，我没有温暖的外壳可以插入。”

blocks.html_en: A Microsoft spokesperson said: “Over several decades, Microsoft has built a global infrastructure to meet rapidly growing customer demand for cloud and AI services. Our datacentres combine custom silicon, AMD, Intel and Nvidia chips across multiple generations with the networking, storage and systems infrastructure required to operate at scale.

sentences.en: A Microsoft spokesperson said: “Over several decades, Microsoft has built a global infrastructure to meet rapidly growing customer demand for cloud and AI services.
sentences.zh: 微软发言人表示：“几十年来，微软已经构建了全球基础设施，以满足客户对云和人工智能服务快速增长的需求。

sentences.en: Our datacentres combine custom silicon, AMD, Intel and Nvidia chips across multiple generations with the networking, storage and systems infrastructure required to operate at scale.
sentences.zh: 我们的数据中心将多代定制芯片、AMD、英特尔和 Nvidia 芯片与大规模运营所需的网络、存储和系统基础设施相结合。

blocks.html_en: “Microsoft does not report on the volume of specific chips in its AI infrastructure. The estimates the Guardian has shared with us are inaccurate, drawing the wrong conclusions from incorrect assumptions.”

sentences.en: “Microsoft does not report on the volume of specific chips in its AI infrastructure.
sentences.zh: “微软没有报告其人工智能基础设施中特定芯片的数量。

sentences.en: The estimates the Guardian has shared with us are inaccurate, drawing the wrong conclusions from incorrect assumptions.”
sentences.zh: 《卫报》与我们分享的估计是不准确的，从错误的假设中得出了错误的结论。”

blocks.html_en: Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.

sentences.en: Nvidia did not respond to a request for comment.
sentences.zh: 英伟达没有回应置评请求。

blocks.html_en: How to calculate numbers of chips from a company’s ‘AI capacity’

sentences.en: How to calculate numbers of chips from a company’s ‘AI capacity’
sentences.zh: 如何根据公司的“AI能力”计算芯片数量

blocks.html_en: The world’s biggest technology companies give figures for their AI capacity in terms of power: gigawatts. One gigawatt powers between 700,000 and 1m homes. Meta says its controversial Hyperion datacentre in Louisiana will have 5GW of capacity. The UK company DataVita is planning a 1GW datacentre in Lanarkshire.

sentences.en: The world’s biggest technology companies give figures for their AI capacity in terms of power: gigawatts.
sentences.zh: 世界上最大的科技公司给出的人工智能容量数据是用功率来表示的：千兆瓦。

sentences.en: One gigawatt powers between 700,000 and 1m homes.
sentences.zh: 1 吉瓦可为 700,000 至 100 万户家庭供电。

sentences.en: Meta says its controversial Hyperion datacentre in Louisiana will have 5GW of capacity.
sentences.zh: Meta 表示，其位于路易斯安那州备受争议的 Hyperion 数据中心将拥有 5GW 的容量。

sentences.en: The UK company DataVita is planning a 1GW datacentre in Lanarkshire.
sentences.zh: 英国公司 DataVita 计划在拉纳克郡建设一座 1GW 的数据中心。

blocks.html_en: Converting these figures into chips means calculating how many chips can be run with that amount of power. The Guardian used the following methodology, reviewing these calculations with Abdeltawab Hendawi, a professor at the University of Rhode Island, and Ren.

sentences.en: Converting these figures into chips means calculating how many chips can be run with that amount of power.
sentences.zh: 将这些数字转换成芯片意味着计算在该功率下可以运行多少芯片。

sentences.en: The Guardian used the following methodology, reviewing these calculations with Abdeltawab Hendawi, a professor at the University of Rhode Island, and Ren.
sentences.zh: 《卫报》使用以下方法，与罗德岛大学教授 Abdeltawab Hendawi 和 Ren 一起审查了这些计算。

blocks.html_en: To get a very broad approximation of how many chips there are in a datacentre, you could divide the power usage of that datacentre by the power usage of an AI chip – for example, an H100. A single H100 uses 700W. If Microsoft has 10GW of capacity, dividing this by 700 watts suggests it should have 12m chips.

sentences.en: To get a very broad approximation of how many chips there are in a datacentre, you could divide the power usage of that datacentre by the power usage of an AI chip – for example, an H100.
sentences.zh: 要获得数据中心中有多少芯片的大致近似值，您可以将该数据中心的用电量除以 AI 芯片（例如 H100）的用电量。

sentences.en: A single H100 uses 700W.
sentences.zh: 单个H100使用700W。

sentences.en: If Microsoft has 10GW of capacity, dividing this by 700 watts suggests it should have 12m chips.
sentences.zh: 如果微软拥有 10GW 的产能，则将其除以 700 瓦表明它应该拥有 1200 万个芯片。

blocks.html_en: H100s make up the bulk of the chips described in the internal document. It also indicates that Microsoft has A100s, which use less power, and Blackwells, which use more.

sentences.en: H100s make up the bulk of the chips described in the internal document.
sentences.zh: H100 构成了内部文档中描述的大部分芯片。

sentences.en: It also indicates that Microsoft has A100s, which use less power, and Blackwells, which use more.
sentences.zh: 它还表明微软有A100，它使用的电量较少，而Blackwells，它使用的电量较多。

blocks.html_en: But this approximation does not account for several factors. First, datacentres have cooling systems and other equipment, which also use electricity. Ren estimates that in a given AI datacentre, 80% of the electricity goes to computer chips. This is roughly in accordance with figures from the International Energy Agency, although the number depends on the efficiency of the datacentre. Eighty per cent of 10GW would suggest 8GW may actually be in use.

sentences.en: But this approximation does not account for several factors.
sentences.zh: 但这种近似并未考虑多种因素。

sentences.en: First, datacentres have cooling systems and other equipment, which also use electricity.
sentences.zh: 首先，数据中心有冷却系统和其他设备，这些设备也使用电力。

sentences.en: Ren estimates that in a given AI datacentre, 80% of the electricity goes to computer chips.
sentences.zh: Ren 估计，在给定的人工智能数据中心，80% 的电力都用于计算机芯片。

sentences.en: This is roughly in accordance with figures from the International Energy Agency, although the number depends on the efficiency of the datacentre.
sentences.zh: 这与国际能源署的数据大致一致，尽管该数字取决于数据中心的效率。

sentences.en: Eighty per cent of 10GW would suggest 8GW may actually be in use.
sentences.zh: 10GW 中的 80% 意味着 8GW 可能实际投入使用。

blocks.html_en: This is slightly lower than Microsoft’s own figures for its datacentre efficiency, which appear in a 2024 sustainability report and suggest that 89% of the electricity in its new datacentres powers the IT systems, with an 11% overhead.

sentences.en: This is slightly lower than Microsoft’s own figures for its datacentre efficiency, which appear in a 2024 sustainability report and suggest that 89% of the electricity in its new datacentres powers the IT systems, with an 11% overhead.
sentences.zh: 这略低于微软自己的数据中心效率数据，该数据出现在 2024 年可持续发展报告中，并表明其新数据中心 89% 的电力为 IT 系统供电，开销为 11%。

blocks.html_en: Second, not all the chips in a datacentre are AI chips. Instead, AI chips are fitted on to server racks with other computer chips, such as memory chips, that help them run calculations. A server with eight H100 GPUs uses a maximum of about 10kW of power.

sentences.en: Second, not all the chips in a datacentre are AI chips.
sentences.zh: 其次，并非数据中心中的所有芯片都是人工智能芯片。

sentences.en: Instead, AI chips are fitted on to server racks with other computer chips, such as memory chips, that help them run calculations.
sentences.zh: 相反，人工智能芯片与其他计算机芯片（例如内存芯片）一起安装在服务器机架上，帮助它们运行计算。

sentences.en: A server with eight H100 GPUs uses a maximum of about 10kW of power.
sentences.zh: 配备 8 个 H100 GPU 的服务器最多使用约 10kW 的功率。

blocks.html_en: Dividing 8GW by 10kW gives 800,000 servers, or 6.4m chips.

sentences.en: Dividing 8GW by 10kW gives 800,000 servers, or 6.4m chips.
sentences.zh: 8GW 除以 10kW 得出 800,000 台服务器，或 640 万块芯片。

blocks.html_en: This is a conservative estimate, as in practice companies such as Microsoft oversubscribe their power capacity to some extent – putting more chips in a datacentre than can be supported by their IT capacity, said Ren.

sentences.en: This is a conservative estimate, as in practice companies such as Microsoft oversubscribe their power capacity to some extent – putting more chips in a datacentre than can be supported by their IT capacity, said Ren.
sentences.zh: 任正非表示，这是一个保守的估计，因为实际上像微软这样的公司在某种程度上超额认购了他们的电力容量——在数据中心放置的芯片数量超出了他们的IT容量所能支持的数量。

content_html_zh:
这些芯片非常小，有些可以握在手掌上。 它们是人工智能模型开发的基础——世界上最大的科技公司需要大量的它们来保持领先地位。

微软就是其中之一。 而且，从纸面上看，它似乎有问题。 《卫报》的一项调查发现，该公司对其人工智能能力的描述与其所运行的先进人工智能芯片的数量之间存在明显差异。

这也不是一个小缺口。 据报道，微软的目标是到 2024 年底在全球数据中心安装 180 万块人工智能芯片。 根据《卫报》看到的内部文件，近两年过去了，在 2800 亿美元（2080 亿英镑）的扩张过程中，该公司已安装了 220 万个人工智能芯片。 这还不到一些专家想象的数字的一半。

简而言之，全球人工智能军备竞赛需要大规模建设运行在极其昂贵的芯片上的数据中心。 芯片上的明显差异表明微软最新的数据中心可能无法完全运行，或者即使可以运行，他们也没有所需的芯片。

这突显了绘制人工智能技术发展进展的更基本的东西。 为人工智能提供动力的芯片是由世界上最有价值的两家公司之一的英伟达制造的。 它的供应链是整个行业最严格保守的秘密之一。

几乎无一例外，英伟达都没有报告其销售了多少这些芯片或卖给了谁。 它的客户是世界上最大的科技公司，但他们却没有透露他们拥有多少家公司。 如果没有这些信息，任何人都很难知道人工智能是否正在蓬勃发展。

微软：权力真空？

微软表示，在过去的两年里，它以极快的速度构建了人工智能基础设施。 其首席执行官萨蒂亚·纳德拉 (Satya Nadella) 去年表示，到 2027 年中期，其全球数据中心足迹将增加一倍。 自 2022 年以来，它已向土地、建筑物和计算基础设施投入了约 2800 亿美元来构建人工智能。 其中包括上一季度超过 410 亿美元的资金。

但很难估计微软用这笔钱建造了多少个数据中心。

通过查看该公司公开宣布的内容，特别是其所需的电力，可以评估该公司正在取得的进展。 数据中心需要电力，因此估计有多少个数据中心正在运行的一种方法是将微软拥有的能源（即人工智能能力）相加。

微软在年度报告和季度收益中声称，作为人工智能建设的一部分，它在过去两年中增加了 5GW 的数据中心容量。 该公司表示，目前在五大洲拥有数百个数据中心。

5 吉瓦的能源量令人眼花缭乱，是欧洲最大数据中心园区面积的四倍。 但微软的总能力应该比这个还要大；自2022年以来，它一直在建设人工智能基础设施。 多大是一个悬而未决的问题。

据报道，在 2024 年的内部演示中，微软声称已经安装了 5GW 的数据中心容量。 这意味着它现在的总产能可能达到 10GW。 目前尚不清楚所有这些是否都是人工智能数据中心——有些可能用于其他云服务。 但微软自己的声明表明，近年来其资本支出的压倒性重点是建设人工智能基础设施。

10 吉瓦的人工智能数据中心意味着微软应该拥有大约 640 万个图形处理单元 (GPU)。 加州大学河滨分校教授任少雷表示，微软的可持续发展报告包含了用电量数据，并且与财务数据分开发布，描绘了一幅不同的画面。

他表示，这些报告表明微软 2024 年的人工智能产能可能接近 1.2GW。 但即使这个较低的数字也表明微软将需要大约 400 万个 AI 芯片——如果它在过去两年增加 5GW 的 AI 数据中心。

“根据他们自己的指标，微软可能是正确的。 但当他们说增加了数据中心容量时，尚不清楚他们的意思。 他们没有提供足够的背景信息，”任说。 “可持续发展报告由第三方审核。 它们比公告更有可信度。”

一位专门研究英伟达的分析师表示，鉴于微软的公开声明，他们认为微软将拥有更多芯片。 “他们对我来说很低。 它们比我预期的微软要少，”他们说。

微软坚称《卫报》的计算基于不正确的信息。 它没有提供任何关于《卫报》的哪些数字不正确或原因的见解。 显而易见的是，微软人工智能能力的建设速度似乎比其年度报告显示的要慢得多。

任正非表示：“理论上，在一个季度内确保或宣布 1GW 的电力装机容量可能是合理的。 但在同一季度内将该容量上线并实际用于计算将会困难得多。”

微软内部消息人士称，该公司的人工智能芯片总数在过去一年“几乎没有变化”。

一些明显的差异可能是由于微软与 OpenAI 的合作造成的。 他们商业合作伙伴关系的具体条款并未公开，但该部门可能负责微软的一些数据中心部署，而《卫报》看到的文件中并没有这些内容。

“你可能有一堆筹码…… 你无法插入”

还有另一个因素：微软的一些大型项目似乎远未投入运营。

以微软在美国最大的人工智能开发项目为例，位于威斯康星州和佐治亚州的两个名为 Fairwater 的数据中心。 四月，微软首席执行官纳德拉表示，威斯康星州的 Fairwater 项目“即将上线”。

然而，Epoch AI 拍摄的该建筑的卫星镜头似乎表明，该建筑仅部分可用。 今年五月，微软向威斯康星州一家报纸承认，Fairwater 尚未上线。

任正非说，这种情况很常见。 最初这是一项数千兆瓦、数十亿美元的投资。 三年后，仅建成300MW。

内部文件还表明，微软拥有的英伟达最新型号的芯片 Blackwell 数量比英伟达公开声明中的预期要少。 去年 3 月，Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 表示，Nvidia 四大客户（普遍认为是亚马逊、甲骨文、微软和谷歌）对 Blackwells 的订单达到 360 万台。

虽然没有给出这个数字的详细数据，但微软历来是英伟达最大的客户之一。 如果情况仍然如此，那么微软持有的 Blackwell 芯片总数应该接近 100 万块。 事实上，它的安装量还不到这个数量的一半。

如果芯片不在数据中心，那么芯片在哪里？

英伟达的资产负债表似乎表明它已经售出了大量芯片；该公司 2 月份营收为 2159 亿美元。 微软购买了这些但没有安装它们吗？ 有多少，全部都在它的手里吗？

纳德拉似乎在去年年底的一个名为 All Things AI 的播客中对这个问题做出了手势，他在其中谈到了微软的数据中心建设。 他说，最大的问题是电力和在距离电力所在地足够近的地方建造数据中心。

“如果你做不到这一点，你的库存中可能实际上有一堆我无法插入的芯片。 事实上，这就是我今天的问题。 这不是芯片供应问题。 事实上，我没有温暖的外壳可以插入。”

微软发言人表示：“几十年来，微软已经构建了全球基础设施，以满足客户对云和人工智能服务快速增长的需求。 我们的数据中心将多代定制芯片、AMD、英特尔和 Nvidia 芯片与大规模运营所需的网络、存储和系统基础设施相结合。

“微软没有报告其人工智能基础设施中特定芯片的数量。 《卫报》与我们分享的估计是不准确的，从错误的假设中得出了错误的结论。”

英伟达没有回应置评请求。

如何根据公司的“AI能力”计算芯片数量

世界上最大的科技公司给出的人工智能容量数据是用功率来表示的：千兆瓦。 1 吉瓦可为 700,000 至 100 万户家庭供电。 Meta 表示，其位于路易斯安那州备受争议的 Hyperion 数据中心将拥有 5GW 的容量。 英国公司 DataVita 计划在拉纳克郡建设一座 1GW 的数据中心。

将这些数字转换成芯片意味着计算在该功率下可以运行多少芯片。 《卫报》使用以下方法，与罗德岛大学教授 Abdeltawab Hendawi 和 Ren 一起审查了这些计算。

要获得数据中心中有多少芯片的大致近似值，您可以将该数据中心的用电量除以 AI 芯片（例如 H100）的用电量。 单个H100使用700W。 如果微软拥有 10GW 的产能，则将其除以 700 瓦表明它应该拥有 1200 万个芯片。

H100 构成了内部文档中描述的大部分芯片。 它还表明微软有A100，它使用的电量较少，而Blackwells，它使用的电量较多。

但这种近似并未考虑多种因素。 首先，数据中心有冷却系统和其他设备，这些设备也使用电力。 Ren 估计，在给定的人工智能数据中心，80% 的电力都用于计算机芯片。 这与国际能源署的数据大致一致，尽管该数字取决于数据中心的效率。 10GW 中的 80% 意味着 8GW 可能实际投入使用。

这略低于微软自己的数据中心效率数据，该数据出现在 2024 年可持续发展报告中，并表明其新数据中心 89% 的电力为 IT 系统供电，开销为 11%。

其次，并非数据中心中的所有芯片都是人工智能芯片。 相反，人工智能芯片与其他计算机芯片（例如内存芯片）一起安装在服务器机架上，帮助它们运行计算。 配备 8 个 H100 GPU 的服务器最多使用约 10kW 的功率。

8GW 除以 10kW 得出 800,000 台服务器，或 640 万块芯片。

任正非表示，这是一个保守的估计，因为实际上像微软这样的公司在某种程度上超额认购了他们的电力容量——在数据中心放置的芯片数量超出了他们的IT容量所能支持的数量。
